name: Certificate Generator
description: Self-sign a certificate, or have a CA issue a leaf certificate from a private key (optionally with a CSR).

examples.label: Issue a leaf certificate from the test CA

hints.keyid: SKID / AKID are added automatically: in CA mode the leaf AKID is taken from the issuer certificate.
hints.mismatch: In CA mode the issuer key must match the issuer certificate, otherwise a key mismatch error is returned.
hints.serial: An empty serial is generated at random; the ceiling is 8 bytes (upstream stores it in a 64-bit integer).

faq.q: What is the difference between self-signed and CA-issued?
faq.a: With self-signing the subject and issuer are the same name and the signer is the new certificate's own key.

faq.q: Can the generated certificate go straight into production?
faq.a: Self-signed certificates are for internal or test use; public services should use a trusted CA.

faq.q: Why is there a serial length limit?
faq.a: Upstream carries the serial in a 64-bit integer, so values longer than 8 bytes cannot be expressed.
